title: Sectionwise module pasting for direct-image composition and open restriction
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On small representatives of the small pro-etale sites of schemes in a common universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and $\mathcal M_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$. Use the module direct images $a_*$, inverse images $a^*$ and their specified adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and the exact open extension by zero $j_!\dashv j^*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Assume the canonical coefficient maps $\alpha_a:a^{-1}\Lambda_T\to\Lambda_S$ are isomorphisms for the morphisms under consideration; identify module inverse image with sheaf inverse image whose action is transported by $\alpha_a^{-1}$.
For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, write $c_{g,f}:(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_*f_*$ for the inverse of the specified module composition isomorphism; its underlying map is restriction along the canonical fibre-product isomorphism [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]. For $f:S\to T$ and an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, put $S_U=S\times_TU$, with maps $j_S:S_U\hookrightarrow S$ and $f_U:S_U\to U$. Let $\beta_{f,j}:j^*f_*\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_U)_*j_S^*$ be the open-slice comparison of [lem-sfb-proetale-open-restriction-counit], initially over actual inverse-image rings and then transported by the coefficient isomorphisms. Then these are natural module isomorphisms with the following simultaneous normalization and coherence.

(a) For every module $M$ on $S$ and site object $V\to U$, $\beta_{f,j,M}(V)$ is the canonical identification $M(S\times_TV)\cong M(S_U\times_UV)$, hence the identity after the canonical identification of fibre products. The action is that obtained from $\alpha_j^{-1}$ and $\alpha_{j_S}^{-1}$. The transformations $c$ and $\beta$ are the lifts of these underlying sheaf maps, including their specified coefficient actions.

(b) For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hT$, one has
$$ (h_*c_{g,f})\circ c_{h,gf}=(c_{h,g}f_*)\circ c_{hg,f}. $$

(c) For successive opens $W\xrightarrow vU\xrightarrow jT$, put $S_W=S\times_TW$ and let $v_S:S_W\hookrightarrow S_U$ be the pulled-back open. Under the canonical comparisons $(jv)^*\cong v^*j^*$ and $j_{S_W}^*\cong v_S^*j_S^*$, one has
$$\beta_{f,jv}=(\beta_{f_U,v}j_S^*)\circ(v^*\beta_{f,j}).$$
Here $j_{S_W}:S_W\hookrightarrow S$ is the composite open.

(d) For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gT$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, put $Y_U=Y\times_TU$, $X_U=X\times_TU$, with opens $j_Y,j_X$ and restricted maps $g_U,f_U$. Then
$$((g_U)_*\beta_{f,j_Y})\circ(\beta_{g,j}f_*)\circ(j^*c_{g,f})=(c_{g_U,f_U}j_X^*)\circ\beta_{gf,j}.$$
All equations include the canonical functor associators and fibre-product identifications. The identity-morphism and identity-open comparisons are identities under their canonical unit identifications. The equations are equalities of module morphisms, not just underlying abelian-sheaf maps, and hold degreewise for every cochain complex with their differentials [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No derived-category assertion, properness or finite/discrete-coefficient hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text:
Work on the small representatives in the statement. Use the sheafified sectionwise tensor on abelian sheaves: [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] supplies strong monoidal sheafification. Thus the size and monoidal-sheafification hypotheses of [lem-sfb-section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence] hold. Apply its internal/sectionwise comparison to each base-change functor, which defines direct image by [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]. In these coordinates
$$(a_*M)(V)=M(S\times_TV),\qquad r\cdot m=\eta_{a,V}(r)m\quad(a:S\to T).$$
This uses the canonical lax structure specified in that comparison; it does not assume that evaluation preserves tensor products. The comparison preserves underlying sheaves and sections. Module morphisms are underlying sheaf morphisms satisfying one action equation by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; consequently equality can be checked on every section over every site object, and a fixed underlying sheaf map has at most one lift.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; internal/sectionwise passage is the explicitly cited existing tensor refinement.

proof.text: The isomorphism [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp] has the underlying sheaf compositor specified in [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]; take its inverse to obtain exactly $c_{g,f}$ in the question. Its evaluation is the reindexing from $M(X\times_ZV)$ to $M(X\times_Y(Y\times_ZV))$. These schemes are canonically isomorphic over $X$, with the same projection to $V$. Naturality in $V$ follows because the reindexing isomorphism commutes with both projections after any arrow $V'\to V$; naturality in $M$ is the naturality of a sheaf morphism for this arrow. Thus no new choice of composition map is made.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; direct-image composition evaluated on base changes.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison] to identify inverse image along an open $j$ with slice restriction over the actual inverse-image ring. The left Kan-extension adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] sends a section of $F(V)$ under its unit to the coprojection indexed by $(V,\mathrm{id}_{U\times_TV})$. For $V\to U$, the canonical slice comparison evaluates this coprojection by restriction along $U\times_TV\to V$, an isomorphism whose inverse is the distinguished lift $V\to U\times_TV$. Thus this unit is identity on $F(V)$ after the canonical identification. The mate formula [def-sfb-eta] therefore identifies $\eta_{j,V}$ with $\alpha_{j,V}:\Lambda_T(V)\to\Lambda_U(V)$; the same holds for every pulled-back open. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], scalar extension along $\alpha_j$ identifies $j^*N$ with $j^{-1}N$, with action $r\cdot n=\alpha_j^{-1}(r)n$: the mutually inverse maps are $n\otimes r\mapsto\alpha_j^{-1}(r)n$ and $n\mapsto n\otimes1$. They commute with restrictions by the balancing relation.

source.place: Tags 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, and 03DH, section-localize; sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize.

proof.text:
Fix $V\to U$ and put $A=S\times_TV\cong S_U\times_UV$. Write $a_V=\alpha_{j,V}$ and $b_A=\alpha_{j_S,A}$ in the slice coordinates of step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-eta-comp] to $j\circ f_U=f\circ j_S$, and evaluate at $V$, regarded as an object over $T$. Its compositors are the fibre-product reindexings of step 2. Step 3 identifies the two open coefficient maps with $a_V,b_A$, so equality of the coefficient maps for this same composite gives
$$b_A\circ\eta_{f,V}=\eta_{f_U,V}\circ a_V.$$
Both $a_V$ and $b_A$ are invertible by hypothesis. Hence for $r\in\Lambda_U(V)$,
$$\eta_{f,V}(a_V^{-1}r)=b_A^{-1}(\eta_{f_U,V}(r)).$$
The left side is the scalar acting on $(j^*f_*M)(V)$; the right side is the scalar acting on $((f_U)_*j_S^*M)(V)$, by steps 1 and 3. Thus the fibre-product reindexing preserves the specified module actions, rather than only the underlying additive groups.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; coefficient-square calculation using the existing composition theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proetale-open-restriction-counit] with $R=\Lambda_T$ and with $M$ first regarded as an $f^{-1}\Lambda_T$-module through $\alpha_f$. It supplies a natural isomorphism on actual inverse-image module sheaves whose evaluation is $M(S\times_TV)\cong M(S_U\times_UV)$. Change the coefficient actions to $\Lambda_U$ and $\Lambda_{S_U}$ using their given isomorphisms. Step 4 proves that exactly this same additive comparison is linear for the resulting actions. Its inverse is linear as well: for a bijective linear map $u$, applying $u$ to $u^{-1}(rn)$ and $r u^{-1}(n)$ gives $rn$ in both cases. Thus it is a natural module isomorphism. It is the transported comparison specified in the statement, and step 1 gives uniqueness of the lift. This proves (a), including the normalization; the composition lift was fixed in step 2.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism, together with sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize; apply the existing module open-slice comparison, then the explicit action calculation.

proof.text:
For (b), evaluate both composites at $M$ and $V\to T$. Their common source is $M(X\times_TV)$ and their common target is
$$M\bigl(X\times_Y(Y\times_Z(Z\times_TV))\bigr).$$
Each is the restriction of $M$ along the canonical map from the latter iterated fibre product to $X\times_TV$. On schemes, both maps have projection to $X$ equal to the first projection and projection to $V$ equal to the iterated last projection. They are equal by the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Contravariant functoriality of $M$ therefore makes the two section maps equal. Since the maps are module morphisms by step 2, step 1 gives the claimed module equality, with the canonical functor associator inserted.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; elementary associativity of base-change reindexing.

proof.text: For successive opens $W\xrightarrow vU\xrightarrow jT$, the canonical module pullback comparison in [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] becomes identity on section groups under the transported-action coordinates of step 3. Indeed, [lem-sfb-eta-comp] evaluated at $E\to W$ gives $\alpha_{jv,E}=\alpha_{v,E}\alpha_{j,E}$, since all three maps are open coefficient maps as computed in step 3. Thus the action transported in one step and the action transported twice coincide: $(\alpha_v\alpha_j)^{-1}=\alpha_j^{-1}\alpha_v^{-1}$. The scalar-extension comparison sends $1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ to $1\otimes m$ and hence is identity in these coordinates. It is the specified comparison: both this map and the comparison defined by conjugation carry the composite scalar-extension unit $m\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ to $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, and the adjunction bijection determines the comparison uniquely. The same argument applies to the two pulled-back opens in $S$.

source.place: Tags 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, and 03DH, section-localize; elementary tensor-unit normalization of the specified comparison.

proof.text:
For (c), let $E\to W$ be any site object. Step 7 identifies the sources for the single and successive restrictions with $M(S\times_TE)$, and identifies their targets with $M(S_W\times_WE)$. By step 5 the single restriction uses the canonical map $S_W\times_WE\to S\times_TE$. The successive restrictions use the composite
$$S_W\times_WE\longrightarrow S_U\times_UE\longrightarrow S\times_TE.$$
The projections to $S$ and $E$ of this composite are the same as those of the single map, so [def-pc-fibre-product] makes them equal. Functoriality of the restrictions of $M$ proves equality on sections. Step 1 makes it an equality of module morphisms with the canonical comparisons of step 7.

For (d), evaluate at $M$ and $V\to U$. The common source is $M(X\times_TV)$, and the common target is
$$M\bigl(X_U\times_{Y_U}(Y_U\times_UV)\bigr).$$
The left-hand path first expands $gf$ through $Y$ and then restricts through $Y_U$ and $X_U$; the right-hand path first restricts $X$ to $X_U$ and then expands $g_Uf_U$. By steps 2 and 5 each path is reindexing along its composite map from $X_U\times_{Y_U}(Y_U\times_UV)$ to $X\times_TV$. Both composites have projection to $X$ induced by $X_U\to X$ and projection to $V$ the last projection. The uniqueness clause of [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies these maps. Contravariant functoriality gives equality on sections, and step 1 gives equality of module morphisms. This also specifies explicitly the fibre-product identifications implicit in (d).

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism, with sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize; mixed pasting calculation.

proof.text: For identity scheme maps, [lem-sfb-eta-id] identifies the coefficient unit with the inverse of the canonical direct-image identity. Therefore the identity direct image has the original module action under $T\times_TV\cong V$. The corresponding composition maps of step 2 are identities in these coordinates. For the identity open, step 3 identifies its coefficient map with this same identity, and step 5 identifies its open comparison with identity. The same projection calculation proves the unit cases when one factor in a composite is an identity. Empty opens and the empty scheme are allowed: all the fibre products in the computations are empty, and the same identities of restriction maps apply.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; identity and unit specializations.

proof.text: Finally let $M^\bullet$ be a cochain complex as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply each comparison to $M^n$ in every integer degree $n$. Naturality in the module morphism $d^n:M^n\to M^{n+1}$, proved in steps 2 and 5, says precisely $B(d^n)\tau_{M^n}=\tau_{M^{n+1}}A(d^n)$ for the two functors $A,B$ compared by $\tau$. Thus the comparisons and their inverses are cochain maps. Every equality already proved is an equality in each degree, hence an equality of these cochain maps. This is exactly the final degreewise assertion; no resolutions or localization are used.
